_comment: Entry contract per state-machine definition: the fields EVERY declared caller
supplies in its StartExecution input, i.e. the INTERSECTION over callers - not
the union. A field only one caller passes is not guaranteed and must not be
listed, or the reachability analysis in infrastructure/sf_reachability.py will
declare a reference safe that a different trigger makes fatal.
against this file. Callers living in another repo are named under
external_callers and are pinned by a consumer-contract test THERE - see

callers: infrastructure/lambdas/saturday-sf-watch-dispatcher/index.py :: fast-path rerun (PASS-THROUGH: replays describe_resp['input'] verbatim, so it can never weaken the contract)
notes: ec2_instance_id is DELIBERATELY absent (alpha-engine-config#2248): the cadence
trigger omits it so CheckSpotDispatchNeeded always engages the fresh-spot
dispatch path instead of pinning the always-on dashboard box. It is produced
inside the graph by MergeWeeklyFreshnessSpotInstanceId, not supplied at entry.
shell_run is passed only by the Friday trigger, so it is NOT in the contract.

Measured 2026-08-28: the weekly graph also analyses clean with an EMPTY entry contract, because InitializeInput's JsonMerge floor supplies every field it reads. These three are still declared because they are what the callers actually guarantee, and a future reference to one of them must not silently become the first thing an operator start can break.
run_date is NOT supplied at entry - InitializeInput stamps it from
$$.Execution.StartTime, which is why this pipeline needs no caller to pass it.
This pipeline has NO InitializeInput defaults floor, so every field here is
load-bearing at entry: 15 states read $.run_date directly and a caller that
omits it raises States.Runtime before any Catch can see it. Verified against
live execution eod-2026-08-28-1787947216, whose input carries all six fields.

This is the ONLY definition whose contract is load-bearing: with an empty contract the EOD graph reports run_date unreachable at 15 states. Giving it an InitializeInput floor like the other two would have to stamp a trading day, not a calendar date (see NormalizeRunDates, alpha-engine-config#8809), so the floor is deliberately NOT copied here - tracked at alpha-engine-config-I9097.

The collector-dependent half of the post-close pipeline, split out of step_function_eod.json 2026-09-30 (alpha-engine-config-I11269 follow-up). Same six-field shape as step_function_eod.json and for the same reason: no InitializeInput floor, and $.run_date is read directly (including WaitForCollectionManifests' {run_date}T20:00:00Z readiness baseline), so a start without it raises States.Runtime before any Catch.

Both of this machine's starters go through _start_reconcile: the collection-terminal event trigger (alpha-engine-eod-reconcile-trigger) and the scheduled reconcile backstop (alpha-engine-eod-reconcile-backstop-daily). The heal loop's HealDispatchReplay self-start is inside the definition, not an in-repo caller file, exactly as it was in the pre-split machine; no state reads $.sns_topic_arn (every SNS target is a hardcoded ARN), so the replay omitting it is not a reachability gap.
EMPTY BY MEASUREMENT, not by omission: the groom graph analyses clean with no
entry contract at all, because every field it reads is produced inside it. The
earlier seed of schedInput/decideMarker was an artefact of the analysis before
it modelled OutputPath and JsonMerge - neither name appears in any caller.
